question: What does India's lower-middle-income label really measure?

theme.label: Economy and public money
readerQuestions: What is the headline economic number?
Is this a total number or a per-person number?
How much of the story is prices, exchange rates, or GDP share?
What does this explain about household life?

plannedCharts.title: India has reached three-fifths of the next income line
plannedCharts.subtitle: Atlas-method GNI per person as a share of each year's upper-middle entry threshold · 1987-2025 · 2025 is an estimate
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: The label is easier to understand as a moving race between India's Atlas income and the threshold it must clear.

plannedCharts.title: India ranks 3rd in PPP output, 132nd in PPP income per person
plannedCharts.unit: World Bank workbook rank · 1 is highest
plannedCharts.subtitle: World Bank 2025 release ranks · PPP GDP among 197 economies; PPP GNI per person among 196 · market GDP among 204; Atlas GNI per person among 200
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: The apparent contradiction disappears when total output and income per person are placed beside each other.

plannedCharts.title: PPP lifts India's per-person figure more than fourfold
plannedCharts.subtitle: PPP GNI per person divided by Atlas GNI per person · India and 11 selected economies · World Bank 2025 estimates
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: The gap between the two rulers is systematic, not an India-only quirk.

plannedCharts.title: The world moved from low income into the middle
plannedCharts.subtitle: Share of people in economies with both a World Bank classification and population estimate · 1987 and 2025
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: The biggest global change since 1987 is the migration of billions into the two middle-income groups.

plannedCharts.title: Half the lower-middle-income population lives in India
plannedCharts.subtitle: Population share within economies classified lower middle income in 2025 · 47 economies with population data
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: The label sounds like a club of similar countries, but its population is dominated by one very large member.

plannedCharts.title: One income label, six very different journeys
plannedCharts.subtitle: Atlas GNI per person divided by each year's upper-middle threshold · India and five Asian comparators · 1987-2025
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Countries can accelerate, stall, cross, or fall back even when they once shared the same category.

plannedCharts.title: Fewer than three in ten peers crossed within a decade
plannedCharts.subtitle: 67 post-1987 lower-middle-income economies first observed at 55-65% of the line · Kaplan-Meier estimate retaining 26 unfinished journeys
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: The full cohort corrects the success bias created by looking only at Asian economies that completed the transition.

plannedCharts.title: Crossing did not stick for 29% of observed movers
plannedCharts.subtitle: Outcome after 76 first observed moves from low or lower middle into upper middle or high income · 1987-2025 history window
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: A global count shows that Indonesia and Sri Lanka are examples of a wider pattern rather than curiosities.

plannedCharts.title: India's GNI rose fast; population, conversion and the threshold absorbed much of it
plannedCharts.subtitle: Sequential accounting identity for India's position relative to the upper-middle line · local-currency GNI, population, Atlas conversion and threshold · 2015-2025
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: The bridge opens India's own classification machinery instead of relying only on stories about countries that moved this year.

plannedCharts.title: Some countries moved because the measurement changed
plannedCharts.subtitle: One-year change in Atlas GNI per person for the six 2025 upward movers · mechanism identified in the World Bank release
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: The 2025 movers expose how growth, recovery, rebasing and population revisions can all change GNI per person.

plannedCharts.title: An upper-middle label would not end World Bank lending
plannedCharts.subtitle: India's Atlas GNI per person beside 2025 analytical income boundaries and separate IDA and IBRD operational thresholds
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Crossing into upper middle income does not automatically end World Bank borrowing or trigger graduation.

plannedCharts.title: India's past gives a 2036-2046 range, not a forecast
plannedCharts.subtitle: Years implied by continuing four historical growth rates in India's ratio to the moving threshold · arithmetic scenarios from 2025
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Several historical windows reveal how sensitive the crossing date is to the pace one chooses.

plannedCharts.title: The income line does not set a child-survival standard
plannedCharts.subtitle: Under-five deaths per 1,000 live births · India 2024 UN IGME estimate versus seven Asian peers in their first upper-middle year
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: A national income label does not guarantee a common level of basic human outcomes.

plannedCharts.title: India has a smaller factory base than most Asian crossers
plannedCharts.subtitle: Manufacturing value added as a share of GDP · India latest available year versus seven Asian peers at first upper-middle classification
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: The route to the same income threshold can rest on very different production structures.

plannedCharts.title: 'Lower middle income' does not describe a typical household
plannedCharts.subtitle: Average monthly consumption per person across rural and urban fractile classes · MoSPI HCES 2023-24 · consumption, not income
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: The national average must end by meeting the distribution it hides.

selectionRules: Start from the page question, not from the indicator name.
Choose the smallest set of visuals that explains scale, trend, structure, comparison, and caveat.
Prefer mobile-friendly charts: line charts with sparse ticks, horizontal bars, share strips, pyramids only when essential, and no dense tables.
Use one strong pull quote only when the evidence supports it with a number.
Add glossary blocks for technical terms that normal readers may not know.
caveats: Use only figures present in lockedNumbers or sourceSummaries.
If a related theme indicator is present, you may use it for context, but do not pretend it is the main answer.
If source coverage is thin, say so directly.
Do not compare states, districts, or cities unless the evidence packet contains those geographies.
forbiddenClaims: Do not infer causality from a trend unless the evidence explicitly supports it.
Do not cite a source that is not present in sourceSummaries.
